newsitem.title: UK: Wlm Cook forecasts 35 pct yr earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: Wlm Cook forecasts 35 pct yr earnings rise.

text.p: British metal castings company William Cook Plc, which is fighting off a hostile takeover bid by engineering group Triplex Lloyd Plc, made an upbeat results forecast for the current year on Thursday, which it said showed how "ludicrously low" the Triplex offer was.

The company said its pretax profit for the year ending March 29, 1997 would rise by not less than 26 percent to 10.7 million stg, while its earnings per share would be up by at least 35 percent to 36.2 pence.
It also saw a 43 percent rise in the final dividend to 9.25 pence, giving a total for the year of 12.0 pence, up 33 percent.
"The forecast is struck before bid defence costs but after refurbishment costs of 2.2 million pounds, which marks the end of William Cook's refurbishment programme," the firm added.
Taking the new figures into account, Cook said, Triplex Lloyd's offer reflected a price earnings ratio of "a paltry 8.5 times, a 43 percent discount to the market (excluding financial companies)".
Triplex Lloyd has made a combined share and cash offer which earlier this month valued William Cook at about 309 pence per share.
In early trading on Thursday, Cook's share price was inidicated at 357-1/2 pence.
